instructions: Put the shiitake in a bowl with 1 cup of hot water and let them soak for 20 minutes while you do the rest of the prep.
Cut the chicken into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Toss them with 1/2 tbsp of the sake and 1/2 tbsp of the soy sauce and leave them in the bowl.
Peel the burdock and slice it thin. Peel the lotus root and cut it into 1/4-inch slices. Put both in a bowl of water with the rice vinegar.

Peel the taro and cut it into bite-size chunks. Peel the carrot and cut it into bite-size chunks at an angle. Drain the bamboo shoots and cut them into bite-size pieces. Cut half of the konnyaku block into 1/2-inch slices.

Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add the konnyaku and boil for 3 minutes. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and set it aside. Add the snow peas to the same water for 30 seconds, then drain and rinse them under cold water.
Lift the shiitake out of their water and squeeze them over the bowl. That should be about 3/4 cup of mushroom liquid. Cut off the stems and throw them away, then halve the caps.
Heat 1 tbsp of the sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, until it's white on the outside. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining 1/2 tbsp sesame oil to the pot. Drain the burdock and lotus root and add them with the shiitake, taro, carrot, bamboo shoots and konnyaku. Stir for 3 minutes.
Stir the dashi granules into 2 cups of hot water. Pour it into the pot with the mushroom liquid. Bring it to a simmer and skim off the foam.
Add 3 tbsp sake, the mirin, sugar, 2 tbsp soy sauce and the salt. Return the chicken to the pot. The liquid should cover about 4/5 of the food.

Cover with a lid set slightly open, or a round of parchment cut to fit, and simmer over medium-low for 10 minutes. Take the cover off and simmer for 10 minutes, until a skewer slides easily into the taro and lotus root.
You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a piece there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the snow peas over the top and serve.

To keep leftovers, let the pot cool, then store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For the freezer, pick out the konnyaku first, since it turns rubbery, and freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a pot over low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook sears the chicken, stir-fries the vegetables in sesame oil, and simmers everything in dashi, sake, mirin, sugar and soy sauce under a drop lid. RecipeTin Eats follows the same order with a shorter vegetable list and a little less seasoning. This one follows Just One Cookbook, with dashi granules for the dashi and the snow peas added at the end. It makes a big pot that keeps for days.
